newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude snaps back, ends slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude snaps back, ends slightly higher.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures, punctuating a volatile session, snapped back from their afternoon losses to close slightly higher on the back of this week's constructive U.S. inventory data and bullish short-term technicals.
April Brent ended 13 cents higher at $19.58 a barrel, trading between $19.30 and $19.84, levels hit during choppy afternoon dealings.
Earlier, March gas oil closed sharply lower, down $3 at $165.75 a tonne and near its fresh eight-month lows, as traders continued to look ahead to the spring season and lower heating oil demand.
"Fund buying early on took us to the highs and then that rally fizzled out," a floor broker said. "There were vacuums in the market that kept appearing because there was not a lot of paper."

Traders said the market was volatile because after a roughly 20 percent drop in prices over the last two months, Brent crude held support at $19 and was able to bounce higher to correct its oversold condition.

Expiry of the NYMEX March products on Friday was also injecting uncertainty, especially after this week's inventory data showed an unexpected drop in U.S. gasoline inventories as the spring season approaches.
